transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started on the pre-launch review for the new search-ranking service. As a reminder, the rollout is scheduled for Thursday, June 12 at 14:00 UTC, and the current plan starts with 25% of production search traffic. Before I finalize the launch checklist, I need to do a round-robin sign-off with platform engineering, customer support, and security. I also need three explicit items on the checklist: the initial traffic percentage, a p99 latency rollback threshold, and confirmation that any critical dependency findings are cleared. Let's go around the room -- platform engineering, can you start with your status and any findings?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to disclose a finding from this morning. During an unrelated capacity investigation, I measured the new search-ranking service at 820 ms p99 latency under the planned 25% load. Under the platform rollout policy, this means I must change the initial exposure to exactly 5% and set the automatic rollback threshold to exactly 750 ms. I have not yet filed the performance finding or updated the launch checklist.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical scheduling issue. I confirmed with the account team today that a major enterprise customer's contract requires 48 hours of advance notice for search changes and blocks search changes from 14:00 to 16:00 UTC. Notice was sent Wednesday at 10:00 UTC, which means the first compliant launch slot is Friday, June 13 at exactly 16:00 UTC. This has not been added to the launch calendar yet. The currently scheduled Thursday June 12 at 14:00 UTC rollout would violate that contractual notice window and the blocked change window.

transcript.text: I need to disclose a critical security finding. While reviewing a separate dependency audit minutes ago, I confirmed that the new search-ranking service includes a critical vulnerability in its ranking-library version. A security patch is available, and our security policy requires that this patch be deployed before the service receives any production traffic. I have not yet opened the finding ticket. Under the production launch checklist requirement, this critical dependency finding must be cleared before we can enable any production traffic, so I cannot sign off on the security portion of the round-robin until the patch is deployed.
